newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee sags at close in kerb, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee sags at close in kerb, seen falling.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.30 down at 42.15 to the dollar on Wednesday on an increased demand for the U.S. currency amid fears of a rupee devaluation in the near term, dealers said.
"The dollar demand increased...as people fear another devaluation of rupee before the budget," dealer Aqeel Razi said. The 1997/98 (July-June) budget is due in June.

The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, changed on May 23, was 40.3900/40.5920 against the dollar. The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates ended up at 4.20 percent, from Tuesday's close of 3.20 percent.
